store.description: Three items in superposition with key capacity 4, three flag bits, seven ticks, joint flags x time.

kernel.description: Apply a weighted kernel in one pass: 1 x identity plus 2 x (flip bit 0 and age one tick).
kernel.cost: One pass over the store; the cost does not depend on the number of kernel elements.
joins: Diffuse (the two-element kernel: stay with weight a, move one tick with weight b minus a)
sums of kernels (Add(PleromaKernel)) and products (PleromaKernel.Compose, block by block)
doesNotJoin: right relabelling of arrangements, and conjugation
bit maps on the flag cube (Frobenius, ShiftRegister)
sign flips of flag words (signs shift the Walsh index)
kernel.rule: A weighted mix of operators that do not join a kernel costs one pass per term. Powers of one such operator compose into one pass.

result.description: 6 + 2 x 6 = 18: the original items plus their flipped and aged copies.

capacityRule.description: A Pleroma with key capacity K keeps 2K+1 harmonics per key line.
capacityRule.implication1: Exact recovery of up to K distinct keys by Berlekamp-Massey syndrome decoding.
capacityRule.implication2: All K items are held at once in one array of 2K+1 entries per key line.
capacityRule.implication3: Past K distinct keys the key reads refuse instead of answering.

cost.conditions: Apply(PleromaKernel) on a 10,464-cell store: GF(13,879), 6 flag bits, S_3, time period 27, joint flags x order x time, key capacity 4, continuous component, 10 items on four keys. Release build, loaded i9-11950H. Random kernels, the mean of 20 calls after one warm-up.
cost.source: PACKAGE.md (superposed operators); PleromaKernelTests OS3 (logged, not asserted)
cost.applyText: 0.17 to 0.44 per call over two runs; no trend from 1 to 10,368 kernel elements.
cost.bruteText: 3 at 1 element; 1,916 at 1,000 elements (building the same store from the moved items).
